answer: Bonded stake resists sybils: each agent must lock a bond before transacting, and misbehavior slashes it, so every fake identity carries a real capital cost instead of a free registration. Like a wharf charging every vessel a berth fee, the gate stays open to honest traders yet makes sockpuppet fleets costly to dock. A zephyr of cheap bots cannot slip through, since ten thousand fakes mean ten thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays once. The limit is wealth bias: a velvet rope of high bonds can price out honest newcomers, so bonds must stay modest and pair with earned reputation.
